To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phase variance over a square pupil is independent of the size of the screen, but the phase variance over an elongated pupil is strongly affected by the size of the simulation.
the phase structure function is sensitive to the format of the phase screen, and that this sensitivity can be eliminated by a simple correction method.

(1) the phase structure function is not symmetric with respect to the diagonal of the phase screen, (2) the phase-structure-function asymmetry is more pronounced for rectangular phase screens than for square phase screens of the same area, and (3) the phase- structure-function asymmetry is reduced for large rectangular phase screens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of rectangular formats and with the compensation for such effects.
the performance of fast-Fourier-transform (FFT)-based simulators of atmospheric phase screens.
the effects of aspect ratio on fast-Fourier-transform simulators of atmospheric turbulence, which have been widely used for the analysis of optical wave propagation in the atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of rectangular formats is not to be recommended.
the phase-structure-function-based methods of analysis of atmospheric wave fronts are not applicable to large rectangular formats.
the aspect ratio is not a problem as long as the size of the rectangular format is large enough.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rectangular phase screen with a size of 1.5 times the size of the pupil is the best choice for a fast Fourier transform simulator with a von Karmán phase screen.

the fast-Fourier-transform method is not a good choice when the aspect ratio of the format is larger than about 2:1, and the size of a phase screen is larger than about two times the size of the largest pupil.
fast-Fourier-transform methods for simulating atmospheric wave fronts can be used with rectangular formats, but the aspect ratio must be taken into consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size of the simulation screen is the most important parameter in the simulation of atmospheric wave fronts.
the size of the simulated phase screen is more critical than its aspect ratio.
the aspect ratio should be taken into account when using fast-fourier-transform methods to simulate large atmospheric wave fronts with high accuracy.
